source: AN 01-60-3 p30 (NAA drawing 106-00001), public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
method: Dark pixels (<140) are closed by 3 px to seal the inked outline, the paper reachable from the crop border is flooded, the complement is opened by 4 px (removes dimension lines, leaders and text) and the largest component is the view's filled silhouette. Manual exclusion boxes (original pixel coordinates) drop closed regions that are not the airplane (dimension boxes, the rudder-travel fan, drop tanks). Each axis of each view is calibrated with a printed dimension because the 1945 reproduction is not isotropic (about 2 %).

side.notes: profile; the main wheel circle is not connected (excluded by the fill); the propeller blade has gaps and is excluded; mask_after removes the vertical propeller blade above and below the spinner from the compared outline

front.notes: left half only (the right wing outline leaks through a dashed line); gear and wheels are dropped by the fill; the four propeller blades cannot be separated from the body by boxes: the front metric is qualitative (wing, stab, gear height)

top.notes: plan; excluded from the FILL: stab dimension box, the rudder 30-degree fan on both sides of the fin (the fin tip column 896-930 is kept), prop-clearance extension box (stopping short of the fuselage side), two drop tanks (their dashed outlines seal under the 3 px closing and would merge with the wing: without the boxes the LE fit residual rises from 0.1 to 2.2 in). review.py ignores outline pixels inside these boxes and removes their area from both masks, so the box edges never count as contour. A 9 px box cuts the stab-span dimension's right extension line, drawn alongside the right stab tip (x 1165): the 3 px closing merged it with the tip and the measured half-span depended on the 2 in sampling grid (79.5 or 81.4 in).
